newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - Bulgarian business weeklies-July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bulgarian business weeklies-July 28.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Deputy Prime Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said the government would ask private firms in Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy to transfer their stakes to state-owned Bulgargas in a bid to restore its 50 percent participation in the joint venture. @

He said that under an intergovernmental agreement between Bulgaria and Russia, only state firms could share Bulgaria's 50 percent stake in Topenergy, and urged Multigroup, Overgas Inc, First Private Bank and Chimimport to transfer their stakes to Bulgargas.
-- Bulgarian commercial banks should raise their capital to ten billion levs by the end of June 1998 to meet new central bank minimum capital requirements. @

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Bulgaria's Bulbank and the U.S. Oppenheimer & Co. Inc bought 99.6 percent of the state-owned United Bulgarian Bank in Bulgaria's first bank privatisation deal.
-- The International Monetary Fund approved the release of a $130 million loan instalment to Bulgaria under a $510 million standby agreement sealed in mid-April.
-- Bulgaria's central bank said it had transferred over $130 million coupon on its Brady bonds to its debt agent on July 25. @

Bulgaria issued on July 28, 1994 three types of Brady bonds with a total par of $5.1 billion as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the so-called London Club of creditor banks.

-- Bulgaria's leasing company Bulgarleasing, in which the state holds 45.8 percent, will be transformed into a holding structure and will raise capital to 100 milion levs from 50 million levs, its shareholders' meeting decided. @
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency has sold 14 enterprises in the last three months, posting proceeds of $248 million. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
